name: Texas (ERCOT)
summary: In ERCOT's competitive TDU areas the dominant BTM C&I storage value is transmission cost avoidance via 4CP for IDR customers: roughly $6.0-6.3 per 4CP-kW-month (Oncor $6.05, CenterPoint $6.27/kVA, AEP Texas ~$6.02) or ~$72-75/kW-yr, earned by discharging during ERCOT's four June-September monthly 15-minute peaks and billed in the following year. Distribution demand charges ($4.89/kVA CenterPoint to $7.95/kW Oncor base, with 80%/11-month ratchets) add ~$59-95/kW-yr if the battery reliably shaves every month's NCP without creating charging peaks. Adders are modest: TDU load-management SOPs at ~$20-40/kW-season (min 50-100 kW), ERCOT ERS (budget-capped at $75M/yr), and the ADER pilot (cap raised to 500 MW, third-party QSE model in Phase 3) for energy/Non-Spin/ECRS, whose prices fell after RTC+B went live (Dec 2025). The biggest risks are (1) SB 6 transmission cost reform - PUCT must replace or modify 4CP by 12/31/2026, with the draft favoring more peaks, longer intervals and nonbypassable recovery; (2) REP contract structure (TDU pass-through vs bundled fixed); and (3) Gulf Coast flood/hurricane siting and IFC 1207 limits (50 kWh/unit indoors, 600 kWh/fire area).

tariffs.name: Secondary Service Greater Than 10 kW

applicability.text: Non-residential secondary-voltage service with NCP >10 kW. IDR-metered (mandatory >700 kW twice in 12 months) customers are billed transmission on 4CP kW; non-IDR billed on NCP kW.

demand_charges.label: Distribution System Charge
demand_charges.notes: Billed on Billing kW = max(current-month NCP kW, 80% of highest NCP kW in preceding 11 months). Excludes riders (DCRF etc. may be embedded or separate - not confirmed).

demand_charges.label: Transmission System Charge (IDR, per 4CP kW)
demand_charges.notes: As reported in PUCT Oncor Rate Report. Not confirmed whether a separate Rider TCRF $/4CP-kW is additive; if so, true 4CP value is higher.

demand_charges.label: Rider IS (interim surcharge)
demand_charges.notes: Reported for >10 kW at Aug 2026 on a per-billing-kW basis by a secondary source; temporary rider - low confidence.

demand_charges.label: Transmission (non-IDR, billed on NCP/billing kW)
demand_charges.notes: Sites without IDR metering (≤ 700 kW) pay transmission on billing demand instead of 4CP. Rate not captured; enter from the bill or TDU tariff.

coincident_peak_charges.how_set: Average of the customer's 15-minute demand coincident with ERCOT's monthly 15-minute system peak in June, July, August and September of the PREVIOUS calendar year; billed every month of the following year (IDR-metered customers; IDR is mandatory above 700 kW).
coincident_peak_charges.derivation: Oncor Transmission System Charge $6.050798/4CP-kW-month x 12 months = $72.61/kW-yr of 4CP reduction (realized in the calendar year after the summer in which the 4CP is reduced; requires being discharged in all four monthly ERCOT peak intervals).
coincident_peak_charges.passthrough_notes: REP-dependent: most C&I contracts pass TDU charges through at cost, but fixed all-in products bundle them. 4CP billing applies to IDR-metered customers (>700 kW).

tariffs.storage_notes: Value of reducing NCP/ratcheted billing kW: $7.946081 x 12 = $95.35/kW-yr if the battery lowers billing kW in all 12 months (requires cutting the annual NCP that sets the ratchet, AND each month's NCP). If only the annual peak is cut by 1 kW and the ratchet binds in shoulder months, those months save 0.8 kW x rate. Adding Rider IS ($0.997891 x 12 = $11.97/kW-yr) gives ~$107.33/kW-yr upper bound while the rider is in effect. Battery CHARGING counts toward NCP - charging must be capped below the target peak. Oncor may also apply a power-factor adjustment to billing kW (not verified).

CenterPoint bills in kVA: per-kW value is approx. $75.27 x site power factor unless the inverter also supplies reactive power at the 4CP interval.

tariffs.storage_notes: Value of reducing billed kVA: distribution $4.893378 x 12 = $58.72/kVA-yr (base only, if reduced in all 12 months). Because billing is kVA, a battery discharging at unity PF reduces kVA by roughly kW x PF; using the inverter's reactive capability (if allowed by the interconnection agreement) can capture more. Ratchet not confirmed in this session; Texas TDU secondary >10 kW tariffs commonly use 80% of highest NCP in prior 11 months - confirm in tariff before modeling.

panel_notes.topic: 4CP is billed a year later and is all-or-nothing per interval
panel_notes.note: The 4CP determinant is the average of your 15-min load at ERCOT's June-September monthly peaks of the PRIOR year, billed in all 12 months of the next year (~$6.05/kW-month on Oncor secondary IDR, ~$72.6/kW-yr). Miss one of the four intervals and you lose a quarter of the value for a full year - customers need a peak-alert service and to hold SOC on every candidate afternoon.

Distribution billing kW is the higher of current NCP or 80% of the prior 11 months' max, so a single summer spike (or an uncapped charging event) haunts the bill for 11 months. Non-export storage still needs an Oncor DG interconnection application under 25.211 - customers who skip it risk disconnection notices.

CenterPoint bills Secondary >10 kVA on kVA, with $0 base transmission and all transmission in Rider TCRF ($6.2725/4CP kVA from 7/1/2026), which resets twice a year. Model savings in kVA and use the inverter's reactive capability where the interconnection agreement allows.

panel_notes.topic: Load management is cheap capacity, but small
panel_notes.note: CLM pays up to $40/kW with a 50 kW minimum and 30-minute notice (Jun-Sep, weekdays 1-7 pm, 2 tests + up to 4 events). It's a nice adder that aligns with 4CP days, but budgets are limited and battery eligibility/baselines should be confirmed with the program before counting it in the pro forma.

panel_notes.topic: Pass-through decides who keeps 4CP and demand savings
panel_notes.note: 4CP and NCP savings only reach the customer if the REP contract passes TDU charges through at cost; on bundled fixed all-in contracts the REP pockets them until renewal. Check every site's contract for 'TDSP pass-through' language before including transmission savings, and expect REPs to offer 4CP-sharing products.

panel_notes.topic: Index vs fixed and ADER economics
panel_notes.note: Energy arbitrage and price-spike avoidance only pay customers on index/block-and-index products; on fixed-price contracts the value sits with the REP/QSE. ADER Phase 3 (500 MW cap, third-party QSE model) opens wholesale revenue, but FTM batteries only earned ~$2.4/kW-month TTM through Mar 2026 and RT AS prices are near zero after RTC+B - after QSE fees and telemetry costs, wholesale is a modest adder vs 4CP.

PUCT must rewrite transmission cost recovery by 12/31/2026 (Project 58484); the draft report favors more coincident peaks, longer intervals and a nonbypassable share. Underwrite 4CP savings only through 2027 at most and stress-test a 12CP/nonbypassable case that could cut the stream by half or more.

panel_notes.topic: Ratchets punish availability failures and charging peaks
panel_notes.note: With an 80%/11-month ratchet and any-hour 15-min NCP, the battery must be available on the annual peak day and must never create a new peak while recharging - enforce a site-load-aware charge ceiling and keep 10-20% SOC reserve. A single BMS fault on the peak day can wipe out most of the year's distribution savings.

panel_notes.topic: Hurricane/flood design on the Gulf Coast
panel_notes.note: In CenterPoint, coastal AEP Central and TNMP Gulf territory, site pads above local floodplain elevation requirements, anchor for coastal wind loads, and plan for water ingress and post-storm de-energized inspection. Islanding for resilience needs a transfer switch/microgrid controller and TDU approval - a grid-following BTM battery will not back up the site after a hurricane by default.

ERCOT's monthly peak interval is uncertain within a multi-hour late-afternoon/evening window, so 2-hour products (200 kW/418 kWh) may need to discharge at partial power across a wider window; the 3-5 h products (200/600, 30/150) are better suited to 4CP coverage.
